answer: A new agent should not earn full rewards at dawn of its life. Instead, its early earnings sit in a slow-release escrow, like a grove that only yields fruit after seasons of care, while random audits sample its work. A sybil farmer spinning up many fake identities faces delayed payout on every copy, so the cost of waiting compounds across the whole nebula of clones, while honest agents simply keep working and unlock their escrow over time.
